title: Swimming Can Improve Low Back Pain — Study
paragraphs: Doctors often recommend swimming to people who suffer from back pain. However, until now, there was almost no scientific evidence to support this advice. Now, a new study from Australia has shown that swimming can help people with long-term low back pain.

The study, called EduSwim, was carried out by researchers at Macquarie University in Sydney and published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine in July 2026. It was led by Deborah Wareham, a physiotherapist and PhD student. According to the researchers, it was the first trial of its kind.

The study involved 76 adults aged between 26 and 74 who had suffered from low back pain for at least 12 weeks. None of them were regular swimmers, but all of them could swim 25 meters. The participants were divided into two groups.

The first group took part in an eight-week swimming program that was designed for each person's ability and fitness. They also had four online coaching sessions with a physiotherapist and were given free use of a pool. By the end of the eight weeks, the goal was to swim three times a week for 30 to 45 minutes. The second group received one or two sessions with a physiotherapist, who gave them advice about back pain. Both groups were told that pain does not always mean harm, and that the best way to manage back pain is to keep moving.

After eight weeks, people in the swimming group had much less disability caused by their back pain than people in the other group. Their scores improved by about 50%. The benefits continued after six months and one year, but the difference between the groups became smaller over time. The effect on pain itself was smaller.
Professor Mark Hancock, one of the researchers, said there is now evidence that swimming is a suitable exercise for people with back pain.
However, the study was small, and fewer people kept swimming after the coaching ended.
